0: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Use this to understand which directories are available before trying to access files. It takes no input parameters and responds with the set of permitted root paths, which is helpful for confirming scope before any read or listing operation is attempted.
1: Click an element on the page. This tool takes a selector that identifies the target element in the current browser page and performs a single mouse click on it. It is typically used to activate buttons, follow links, or trigger interface actions while automating a web session, and it returns once the click has been dispatched.
2: Execute JavaScript in the browser console. This tool accepts a snippet of JavaScript as input and runs it in the context of the currently loaded page, returning the value produced by the script. It is commonly used to read page state or perform small scripted interactions during browser automation.
3: Fill out an input field. This tool takes a selector for a form field together with the text value to enter, then types that value into the identified input on the current page. It is typically used when automating forms, returning once the field has been populated with the provided text.
4: Hover an element on the page. This tool accepts a selector identifying the target element and moves the pointer over it, triggering any hover state or menu the page attaches to that element. It is often used during browser automation to reveal tooltips or dropdowns, and returns once the hover has been applied.
5: Navigate to a URL. This tool takes a destination web address as input and loads that page in the current browser session, waiting for the page to be ready. It is the usual starting point for a browsing task, and it returns once navigation to the requested address has completed.
6: Take a screenshot of the current page or a specific element. This tool optionally accepts a selector; with no selector it captures the full visible page, and with one it captures just that element. It returns the resulting image, which is useful for recording page state during automation.
7: Select an element on the page with Select tag. This tool takes a selector for an HTML select dropdown and the option value to choose, then sets that dropdown to the requested option on the current page. It is typically used when completing forms and returns once the option has been selected.
8: 周边搜，根据用户传入关键词以及坐标location，搜索出radius半径范围的POI。用户需提供搜索关键词、中心点经纬度坐标以及搜索半径，工具会在指定范围内检索匹配的兴趣点，并返回名称、地址与坐标等结果信息，便于查找附近的地点。
9: 骑行路径规划用于规划骑行通勤方案，规划时会考虑天桥、单行线、封路等情况，最大支持 500km 的骑行路线规划。用户需传入起点与终点的经纬度坐标，工具会计算合适的骑行路线，并返回距离、预计耗时与分段导航等通勤方案数据。
10: 驾车路径规划 API 可以根据用户起终点经纬度坐标规划以小客车、轿车通勤出行的方案，并且返回通勤方案的数据。用户需提供起点与终点坐标，工具据此计算行车路线，返回总距离、预计行驶时间以及逐段行驶指引等信息，供驾车出行参考。
11: 公交路径规划 API 可以根据用户起终点经纬度坐标规划综合各类公共（火车、公交、地铁）交通方式的通勤方案，并且返回通勤方案的数据，跨城场景下必须传起点城市与终点城市。工具会综合换乘情况给出线路、时间与票价等数据。
12: 步行路径规划 API 可以根据输入起点终点经纬度坐标规划100km 以内的步行通勤方案，并且返回通勤方案的数据。用户需提供起点与终点的经纬度坐标，工具会计算适合步行的路线，并返回步行距离、预计耗时以及分段步行指引等信息。
13: 距离测量 API 可以测量两个经纬度坐标之间的距离，支持驾车、步行以及球面距离测量。用户需提供起点与终点坐标并指定测量方式，工具据此计算并返回两点之间的距离数值，便于估算出行里程或两地间的直线距离。
14: 将详细的结构化地址转换为经纬度坐标，支持对地标性名胜景区、建筑物名称解析为经纬度坐标。用户输入文字地址或地点名称，工具进行地理编码解析，并返回对应的经度与纬度坐标及匹配信息，便于后续在地图上定位该地点。
15: IP 定位根据用户输入的 IP 地址，定位 IP 的所在位置。用户需提供一个 IP 地址，工具会据此估算该地址对应的大致地理区域，并返回所在的省份、城市等行政区划信息，常用于粗略判断访问来源的所在地。
16: 将一个高德经纬度坐标转换为行政区划地址信息。用户输入一组经度与纬度坐标，工具进行逆地理编码，返回该坐标所对应的结构化地址，包括省、市、区县以及附近的街道或兴趣点等描述信息，便于了解坐标所在位置。
17: 查询关键词搜或者周边搜获取到的POI ID的详细信息。用户需传入某个兴趣点的 POI ID，工具会据此检索该地点的完整资料，并返回名称、地址、经纬度坐标、类别以及联系方式等详细信息，便于进一步了解该地点。
18: 关键词搜，根据用户传入关键词，搜索出相关的POI。用户提供一个搜索关键词，工具会在地图数据中检索名称或类别与之匹配的兴趣点，并返回每个结果的名称、地址与坐标等信息，便于根据文字查找地点。
19: 根据城市名称或者标准adcode查询指定城市的天气。用户需提供城市名称或对应的 adcode 编码，工具据此查询该城市的天气情况，并返回温度、天气状况、风向风力以及湿度等信息，便于了解目标城市的当前或近期天气。
20: Upload an invoice to Adfin given its absolute path. This tool takes the absolute file path of an invoice document on the local system and uploads that file into Adfin for processing. It is typically used to bring billing documents into the platform, and it returns confirmation once the upload has completed.
21: Write note to flomo. This tool takes the text content of a note as input and saves it to the user's flomo account as a new memo. It is typically used to quickly capture a thought or snippet, and it returns once the note has been stored in flomo.
22: Add a comment to an existing issue. This tool takes the repository, the issue number, and the comment text, then posts that comment on the specified GitHub issue. It is typically used to continue a discussion or record an update, and it returns once the comment has been added to the issue.
23: Create a new branch in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository and the name for the new branch, optionally with a source branch to start from, then creates that branch. It is typically used to begin work on a feature or fix, and it returns the details of the newly created branch.
24: Create a new issue in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository along with a title and optional body, labels, and assignees, then opens a new issue there. It is typically used to report a bug or track a task, and it returns the details of the issue that was created.
25: Create or update a single file in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository, file path, content, and a commit message, then writes that file, creating it or replacing its contents. It is typically used to commit one change at a time, and it returns the resulting commit information.
26: Create a new pull request in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository, the head and base branches, and a title with optional description, then opens a pull request proposing those changes. It is typically used to request review and merging, and it returns the details of the new pull request.
27: Create a review on a pull request. This tool takes the repository, the pull request number, and the review body with an event such as approve or request changes, then submits that review. It is typically used during code review, and it returns once the review has been recorded on the pull request.
28: Create a new GitHub repository in your account. This tool takes the repository name along with optional settings such as description and visibility, then creates that repository under your account. It is typically used to start a new project, and it returns the details of the repository that was created.
29: Fork a GitHub repository to your account or specified organization. This tool takes the source repository and an optional target organization, then creates a fork under your account or that organization. It is typically used to start from someone else's project, and it returns the details of the forked repository.
